summary: Incident intake form: require taxonomy fields and enforce on status updates
description:
Background
We are rolling out Incident Taxonomy v1 and need incident metadata to be consistently captured at declaration time and kept consistent when status updates are posted (e.g., /incident update). Today, several incidents are missing category/owner or get updated without those fields, which breaks dashboards and increases paging ambiguity.

Request
Update the incident intake workflow (Slack incident-bot modal + update command) so taxonomy fields are required and validated:
1) On incident declaration: require category + impacted surface + environment/region + initial owner (team/on-call route).
2) On incident status updates: if any of the required taxonomy fields are missing, block the update and prompt the IC/dispatcher to fill them in (or provide a one-click link to the edit modal).
3) Enforce allowed values (picklist) rather than free text.

Minimum required fields (v1)
- Incident Category (taxonomy v1)
- Impacted Surface (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private where applicable + sub-surface if present)
- Environment + region(s)
- Owning team/on-call route (primary)

Notes / constraints
- Must be low-friction for active response. If we block updates, we need a clear escape hatch for unusual incidents (e.g., temporary "Unknown" but still a valid allowed value).
- Must not conflict with existing severity workflow; severity remains required per current incident process.
- Data should land in the same dataset used for incident dashboards and postmortem automation.

Acceptance criteria
- Incident-bot declaration modal fails validation if required taxonomy fields are missing.
- /incident update fails with a clear error message if required taxonomy fields are still missing, and provides a shortcut to set them.
- Allowed values are enforced (no typos / variants).
- Quick verification: create a test incident in #incidents-sandbox and confirm metadata appears in incident export / dashboard feed.

References
- Confluence (draft): Incident categorization policy + metadata standard (see Reliability initiatives: Incident taxonomy v1)
- Linear initiative: ENG-4821 (Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping)
- Related implementation work expected in incident-bot repo.
comments: 2025-01-29 10:14 Rafael Mendes (Reporter): Filed after reviewing last week’s incident threads. We had 3 incidents where status updates went out with blank category/owner, which forced manual follow-up and broke the MTTR-by-category view. Can we make category + impacted surface mandatory at least before the first status update?

2025-01-30 09:02 Devon Price (Assignee): Acknowledged. Plan: (1) add validation to declare modal, (2) add a pre-flight check on /incident update that rejects when required fields are missing, with a link to /incident edit. Will coordinate allowed-values list with Allison (observability standard) + Miles (taxonomy).

2025-02-03 15:27 Allison Grant: Please ensure fields match the allowed values exactly (category enums + impacted_surface enums). We need stable strings for dashboard grouping. Suggest allowing "Unknown" but only for first 15 minutes; after that require a real category (policy question).

2025-02-04 11:18 Rafael Mendes: For v1, okay to allow "Unknown" as an allowed value, but we should block status updates after 15 minutes unless it’s set. If that’s too much for first pass, at minimum block if category is empty, not if it’s Unknown.

2025-02-06 17:41 Devon Price: Implemented: category/impacted surface/owner required on declare. For status updates: if any required fields are empty, update command errors and points to edit modal. Not implementing time-based enforcement in this ticket; will track as follow-up if needed.

2025-02-11 10:05 Devon Price: Shipped behind feature flag "taxonomy_required_fields" and enabled in #incidents-sandbox + production. Verified: status update is blocked when category missing; edit modal opens with required picklists. Marking resolved.
